answer: Keep Sybils out with a lantern-maker's flame test. A newcomer folds 18 lanterns over 22 days. Two lantern-makers from different workshops fit each lantern's 24 ivory paper panels, then hold a flame beneath them for 30 seconds. A lantern that tears voids its credit and pauses folding for 14 days, and three torn lanterns void the tally outright. Faking 1,000 agents means folding 18,000 lanterns and passing 36,000 flame tests, while one honest agent tends a single bench at its own pace. Like copper catching first light on a ridge, trust is earned panel by panel.
